required.quote: The Board shall provide by rule or regulation for continuing education for persons certified to practice medicine or other professions or occupations pursuant to this chapter.

value: At least 2 hours per reporting period on diagnosis, treatment, or care of patients with Alzheimer's disease or other dementias (required for 2027 renewal and after)
topical_requirements.quote: For professionals renewing their license after 2027, the Board must require that the professional have completed at least 2 hours of the total required during that reporting period of continuing education dedicated to the diagnosis, treatment, or care of patients with Alzheimer's disease or other dementias.
topical_requirements.citation: § 1713. Powers and duties of the Board.

available.quote: The applicant for whom the examination is to be waived is licensed, certified, registered, or otherwise legally authorized to practice medicine by competent authority in any other of the United States or in any other jurisdiction approved by the Board.

title_protection.quote: Using the designation Doctor, Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Osteopathy, physician, surgeon, physician and surgeon, Dr., M.D., or D.O., or a similar designation, or any combination thereof, in the conduct of an occupation or profession pertaining to the prevention, diagnosis, or treatment of human disease or condition, unless the designation additionally contains the description of another branch of the healing arts for which one holds a valid license in the State.

scope_protection.quote: A person who practices or attempts to practice medicine contrary to the provisions of this chapter is guilty of a class F felony

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use of false, fraudulent, or forged statements or documents in connection with certification, registration, or licensing requirements, or in connection with the practice of medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The use of any false, fraudulent, or forged statement or document or the use of any fraudulent, deceitful, dishonest, or unethical practice in connection with a certification, registration, or licensing requirement of this chapter
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conduct that would constitute a crime substantially related to the practice of medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conduct that would constitute a crime substantially related to the practice of medicine
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Any dishonorable, unethical, or other conduct likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any dishonorable, unethical, or other conduct likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing medicine under a false or assumed name.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The practice of medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter under a false or assumed name
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing medicine without a certificate or other authorizing document or renewal thereof.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The practice of medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter without a certificate or other authorizing document or renewal of such document, unless otherwise authorized by this chapter
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Using, distributing, or issuing a prescription for a dangerous or narcotic drug other than for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The use, distribution, or issuance of a prescription for a dangerous or narcotic drug, other than for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Advertising the practice of medicine in an unethical or unprofessional manner.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Advertising of the practice of medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter in an unethical or unprofessional manner
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Soliciting or accepting a fee by fraudulent representation that a manifestly incurable condition can be permanently cured.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Solicitation or acceptance of a fee from a patient or other person by fraudulent representation that a manifestly incurable condition, as determined with reasonable medical certainty, can be permanently cured
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly or intentionally assisting an unauthorized person to practice medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Knowing or intentional performance of an act which, unless authorized by this chapter, assists an unauthorized person to practice medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to provide adequate supervision to an individual working under the supervision of a certified and registered physician.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The failure to provide adequate supervision to an individual working under the supervision of a person who is certified and registered to practice medicine
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Misconduct including sexual misconduct, incompetence, or gross negligence or pattern of negligence in the practice of medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Misconduct, including but not limited to sexual misconduct, incompetence, or gross negligence or pattern of negligence in the practice of medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Wilful violation of the confidential relationship with or confidential communications of a patient.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Wilful violation of the confidential relationship with or confidential communications of a patient
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Wilful failure to report to the Board as required by various statutory provisions.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Wilful failure to report to the Board as required by § 1730(a) of this title
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Unjustified failure upon request to divulge information relevant to the authorization or competence of a person to practice medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Unjustified failure upon request to divulge information relevant to the authorization or competence of a person to practice medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter to the Board
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of a provision of this chapter or an order or regulation of the Board that will more probably than not harm or injure the public or an individual.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The violation of a provision of this chapter or the violation of an order or regulation of the Board related to medical procedures or to the procedures of other professions or occupations regulated under this chapter, the violation of which more probably than not will harm or injure the public or an individual
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Charging a grossly exorbitant fee for professional or occupational services rendered.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Charging a grossly exorbitant fee for professional or occupational services rendered
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Suspension or revocation of certificate to practice medicine or disciplinary action taken by a regulatory authority in another state or territory.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Suspension or revocation of a certificate to practice medicine or of the authorizing document to practice another profession or occupation regulated under this chapter, or other disciplinary action taken by the regulatory authority in another state or territory.
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Signing the death certificate of a person prior to the actual time of death.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Signing the death certificate of a person prior to the actual time of death of the person
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in conversion therapy with a child or referring a child to a provider in another jurisdiction to receive conversion therapy.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in conversion therapy with a child; and Referring a child to a provider in another jurisdiction to receive conversion therapy.
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Inability to practice medicine with reasonable skill or safety by reason of mental or physical disability or serious health condition.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A certificate to practice medicine is subject to restriction, suspension, or revocation, either temporarily or permanently, in case of the inability of a physician to practice medicine with reasonable skill or safety to patients by reason of a mental or physical disability or serious health condition
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

establishment_regulation_required.quote: No person licensed under this chapter shall perform any office-based surgery, as defined in § 122(3)y. of Title 16, in a facility unless such facility is accredited or licensed in accordance with § 122(3)z. of Title 16.

definition_quote.value: "Practice of medicine" or "practice medicine" includes: a. Advertising, holding out to the public, or representing in any manner that one is authorized to practice medicine in this State; b. Offering or undertaking to prescribe, order, give, or administer any drug or medicine for the use of another person; c. Offering or undertaking to prevent or to diagnose, correct, and/or treat in any manner or by any means, methods, or devices a disease, illness, pain, wound, fracture, infirmity, defect, or abnormal physical or mental condition of another person, including the management of pregnancy and parturition; d. Offering or undertaking to perform a surgical operation upon another person
definition_quote.quote: "Practice of medicine" or "practice medicine" includes: a. Advertising, holding out to the public, or representing in any manner that one is authorized to practice medicine in this State; b. Offering or undertaking to prescribe, order, give, or administer any drug or medicine for the use of another person; c. Offering or undertaking to prevent or to diagnose, correct, and/or treat in any manner or by any means, methods, or devices a disease, illness, pain, wound, fracture, infirmity, defect, or abnormal physical or mental condition of another person, including the management of pregnancy and parturition; d. Offering or undertaking to perform a surgical operation upon another person

methods_authorized.quote: Offering or undertaking to prevent or to diagnose, correct, and/or treat in any manner or by any means, methods, or devices a disease, illness, pain, wound, fracture, infirmity, defect, or abnormal physical or mental condition of another person

drug_authority.value: Physicians may prescribe, order, give, or administer any drug or medicine. Electronic prescribing is required except in specified exceptions. Prescriptions for dangerous or narcotic drugs must be for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes.
drug_authority.quote: Offering or undertaking to prescribe, order, give, or administer any drug or medicine for the use of another person

license_status_types.quote: The Board may issue an administrative medicine license to a physician who meets all qualifications for licensure

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Foreign medical graduates must hold a degree from a school listed in the International Medical Education Directory (IMED) and pass the ECFMG examination and FSMB examination; or if the school is not listed in IMED, must complete 3 years of ACGME-approved postgraduate training and pass the ECFMG and FSMB examinations. Clinical rotations must be in formally affiliated institutions.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: A degree of Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathy, or an equivalent degree, from a legally incorporated medical college or school located in a country other than the United States or Canada, medical college or school which is listed in the International Medical Education Directory (IMED), along with documentary proof that the applicant successfully passed the examination administered by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates and the Federation of State Medical Boards

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: A degree of Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathy, or an equivalent degree, from a legally incorporated medical college or school located in a country other than the United States or Canada, which medical college or school is not listed in the International Medical Education Directory (IMED), but the applicant has completed 3 years of postgraduate training in a residency program which has been approved by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: Electronic prescriptions are required generally; store-and-forward transfer and telemedicine are recognized as part of practice. Practice of medicine occurs where the patient is located at the time a physician practices medicine upon the person.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: Rendering a written or otherwise documented medical opinion concerning the diagnosis or treatment of a person or the actual rendering of treatment to a person within the State by a physician located outside the State as a result of transmission of the person's medical data by electronic or other means from within the State to the physician or to the physician's agent

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: "Collaborative agreement" means a written document expressing an arrangement of collaboration between a licensed physician and a physician assistant.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: Physician assistants have prescriptive authority for therapeutic drugs and treatments within the scope of physician assistant practice, subject to biennial renewal. They may prescribe medication for termination of pregnancy including Mifeprex, Mifepristone, and Misoprostol.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: Prescriptive authority for therapeutic drugs and treatments within the scope of physician assistant practice. The physician assistant's prescriptive authority and authority to practice as a physician assistant are subject to biennial renewal upon application to the Physician Assistant Regulatory Council

max_physician_assistants_per_supervising.quote: A collaborating physician may not at any given time collaborate with more than 4 physician assistants, unless a regulation of the Board increases or decreases the number.
max_physician_assistants_per_supervising.citation: § 1771. Physician's role in collaborating with a physician assistant.

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: Every person to whom a certificate to practice medicine is issued has a duty to report to the Board, within 60 days, all information concerning medical malpractice claims settled or adjudicated to final judgment
malpractice_reporting_required.citation: § 1730. Duty to report unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: Every person to whom a certificate to practice medicine is issued and health care facility as defined in § 1740 of this title has a duty to report to the Board within 30 days: a. Any partial or full removal of hospital privileges based on adverse events, unprofessional conduct or competency issues
hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.citation: § 1730. Duty to report unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: If the Executive Director reasonably believes that a diagnostic mental or physical examination of the person under investigation is necessary, the Executive Director shall order the person to submit to an examination at the person's expense
compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.citation: § 1732. Investigations of complaints; Executive Director authority.

administrative_medicine_license_availabl.quote: The Board may issue an administrative medicine license to a physician who meets all qualifications for licensure, including payment of a fee set by the Division of Professional Regulation, except that an applicant for an administrative medicine license shall not be required to show that the applicant has been engaged in the active practice of medicine

locum_tenens_permit_available.quote: The applicant for whom the examination is to be waived is licensed, certified, registered, or otherwise legally qualified to practice medicine in another state of the United States or in another jurisdiction, and seeks a temporary certificate to practice medicine for not less than 2 weeks nor more than 3 months for the purpose of taking charge of the practice of a person certified and registered to practice medicine in this State during the person's temporary illness or absence from this State.
locum_tenens_permit_available.citation: § 1722. Waiver of professional examination for temporary certification, for hospital or institution staff, for physicians licensed in another jurisdiction, and for physicians passing an alternative exam.
